title: Sports
description: Ten short stories about sports and exercise: a running club, beach volleyball, a baseball fan, a swimming class, a bike trip, training for a race, a basketball team, a sports center in an old prison, a soccer blog and a fitness test.

lessons.title: The Running Club
lessons.summary: Laura's doctor tells her to exercise, so she joins a running club, and the other members help her.
lessons.text:
My name is Laura. I am 34 years old, and I work in an office in Denver. For a long time, I didn't exercise at all. I sat at my desk all day, and in the evening I sat in front of the TV. I knew that this wasn't healthy, but I didn't know how to change.

Last spring, I went to see my doctor. She told me that I should exercise more. "Exercise has a lot of benefits," she said. "It's good for your heart, and it's good for your mental health too. You shouldn't sit all day. If you exercise 3 times a week, you will feel much better."

A week later, I joined a running club in my neighborhood. The club meets in the park every Tuesday and Thursday at 6 in the evening. Before my first evening, I was totally sure that I couldn't do it. And it was hard. I could only run for 2 minutes, and then I had to walk.

But my fellow club members were very kind. Somebody always ran next to me and talked to me. "You're doing great," they said. "You shouldn't stop. Just walk when you need to, and then run again." Their words really encouraged me.

After a month, I could run for 20 minutes without stopping. After 3 months, I ran 3 miles. I was totally surprised, and my fellow members were happy for me.

Now I know the benefits of exercise. I sleep better, and I have more energy at work. For me, the mental benefits are the biggest. When I have a hard day, a run in the park helps me forget my stress. I feel healthy and happy.

Last week, a new woman came to the club. Her name was Sue, and she looked worried. She told me that she couldn't run for more than a minute. "That's OK," I said. "Somebody encouraged me when I started. Now I will encourage you."

Questions:
What did Laura's doctor tell her?
She told Laura that she should exercise more, because exercise has a lot of benefits.
When does the running club meet?
It meets in the park every Tuesday and Thursday at 6 in the evening.
How long could Laura run on her first evening?
She could only run for 2 minutes, and then she had to walk.
How did her fellow club members help her?
Somebody always ran next to her and encouraged her.
What are the benefits of exercise for Laura?
She sleeps better, she has more energy, and she feels less stress.
What did Laura say to Sue?
She said that she would encourage Sue.

lessons.title: Volleyball on the Beach
lessons.summary: Jenny and her friend Rosa play beach volleyball on a hot Saturday and win after a slow start.
lessons.text:
Jenny lives in San Diego, a city in southern California. The weather in southern California is warm and sunny for most of the year, so many people spend their free time at the beach.

Every Saturday morning, Jenny plays beach volleyball with her friend Rosa. In beach volleyball, there are 2 teams of 2 players. A high net is in the middle, and the players hit the ball over the net with their hands and arms. It is a fast sport, and you have to run and jump a lot.

Jenny has loved this sport since she was 15. She played it twice a week in college, and she still plays twice a week now: on Wednesday evening and on Saturday morning.

This Saturday, the temperature was already 80 degrees at 9 in the morning. The rays of the sun were very strong. Jenny and Rosa brought a lot of fresh water and a bag of fresh fruit.

They played against 2 men from Los Angeles, Tony and Greg. The men were tall, and they had long arms. They hit the ball very hard over the net. They won the first game, 21 to 15.

In beach volleyball, the teams switch sides every 7 points because of the wind and the sun. In the first game, Jenny often had the rays of the sun in her eyes, and she missed some easy balls. Then the teams switched sides again, and the sun was behind her. "Now we can win," Rosa said.

In the second game, Jenny and Rosa played much better. Jenny jumped high at the net and put her arms up. When Tony hit the ball, it hit Jenny's hands and fell on his side of the net. Jenny and Rosa won the second game, and then they won the third game too.

After the games, the 4 players sat under a tree and drank more fresh water. The temperature was now 90 degrees. "That was a wonderful morning," Jenny said. "Volleyball is a wonderful sport." Tony and Greg said that they wanted to play again next Saturday.

Questions:
Where does Jenny live?
She lives in San Diego, a city in southern California.
How often does Jenny play volleyball?
She plays twice a week, on Wednesday evening and on Saturday morning.
What was the temperature at 9 in the morning?
The temperature was already 80 degrees.
Why do the teams switch sides?
They switch sides because of the wind and the sun.
Who won the second game?
Jenny and Rosa won the second game.
What did Tony and Greg say after the games?
They said that they wanted to play again next Saturday.

lessons.title: A Baseball Fan
lessons.summary: Joe, a fan for 4 decades, takes his young son Max to his first baseball game.
lessons.text:
Joe is 52 years old, and he is a big baseball fan. For 4 decades, he has watched almost every game of his team, the Bridgeport Eagles. He went to his first Eagles game in 1982, when he was 8 years old. Now his son Max is 8, and Joe wanted to take him to his first game.

Joe bought 2 prime seats near the field. "These are prime seats," he told Max. "From here, we can see everything." Max was very excited.

The crowd was huge. More than 40,000 fans were there, and most of them wore the team's colors, blue and white.

Then Joe bought the traditional food of baseball: 2 hot dogs. Max also wanted chicken wings, so Joe bought a box of wings too. The wings were hot, and Max loved them.

During the game, Joe told Max about his hero. "When I was a boy, my hero was Sam Carter. He was the most famous player in the country. He played for the Eagles for 2 decades, and he hit more than 500 home runs."

At the end of the game, the score was 3 to 3. Then a young player named Danny Ruiz hit the ball very hard. It flew over the wall for a home run. The crowd raised their arms and shouted. Max raised his arms too, and he jumped up and down. The Eagles won, 4 to 3.

After the game, the fans celebrated outside. Joe and Max celebrated with a big dinner at home. "Dad, I have a hero now," Max said. "It's Danny Ruiz. One day, he will be as famous as Sam Carter."

Joe smiled. He was happy that his son was a baseball fan now too.

Questions:
How long has Joe been a fan of the Eagles?
He has been a fan of the Eagles for 4 decades.
Where were their seats?
They had prime seats near the field.
What is the traditional food of baseball?
The traditional food of baseball is a hot dog.
Who was Joe's hero when he was a boy?
His hero was Sam Carter, the most famous player in the country.
What did the crowd do after Danny Ruiz's home run?
The crowd raised their arms and shouted.
How did Joe and Max celebrate?
They celebrated with a big dinner at home.

lessons.title: Learning to Swim
lessons.summary: Carlos, who is 40, takes a class for adults at the city pool and learns to swim.
lessons.text:
Carlos is 40 years old, and he can't swim. When he was a boy, his family lived far from the sea, and nobody taught him. Last summer, his children played in the lake with their friends, but Carlos had to stay on the beach. He decided that he had to learn.

In September, Carlos started a class for adults at the city pool. The teacher, Kim, has taught swimming for 15 years.

On the first evening, Kim explained the rules. "The pool has 3 zones," she said. "The children's zone is on the left. The deep zone is on the right, and only people who swim well can go there. We will stay in the learning zone in the middle. The water there is only 4 feet deep, so you can always stand up."

"My first duty is to ensure that you are safe," Kim said. "A guard is always on duty here, and I will always be next to you."

The first class was tough for Carlos. Kim showed the group a simple signal. "When I raise my hand, that is the signal," she said. "When you see the signal, put your face in the water and count to 5." When Kim gave the signal, Carlos put his face in the water. He shut his eyes and counted to 5. It was tough, but he did it.

Kim also explained why swimming is important. "It's not only a sport," she said. "It's a skill that can help you survive. If you fall into deep water, you have to keep your head up and stay still. Your body will respond well if you don't fight the water."

Every week, Carlos asked a lot of questions, and Kim responded to every question with a smile. After 2 months, Carlos didn't shut his eyes in the water anymore. After 4 months, he could swim the whole length of the pool. Then he could swim 10 lengths without stopping.

At the last class, Kim said that Carlos was ready for the deep zone. "You did it," she said. "Now you can swim with your children this summer."

Questions:
Why didn't Carlos learn to swim as a boy?
His family lived far from the sea, and nobody taught him.
What are the 3 zones of the pool?
There is a children's zone, a learning zone and a deep zone.
What is Kim's first duty?
Her first duty is to ensure that everyone is safe.
What is the signal?
When Kim raises her hand, that is the signal.
Why is swimming an important skill?
It is important because it can help you survive in deep water.
How many lengths could Carlos swim after 4 months?
He could swim 10 lengths without stopping.

lessons.title: An E-mail from a Bike Trip
lessons.summary: Kate writes to her sister about a bike trip with her husband in northern Michigan.
lessons.text:
Hi Ellen,

I'm writing to you from a small hotel in northern Michigan. As you know, Dave and I are on a bike trip this week. We ride about 40 miles a day, and so far everything has been great.

Our route goes along Lake Michigan. Dave planned the route months ago, and he planned it well. The roads in this northern part of the state are small and safe, and the views of the lake are beautiful.

Before the trip, Dave mounted a small camera on the front of his bike. It is mounted very well, and it records the whole route. When we get home, we can watch the whole trip again.

We have seen a lot of wild animals. Yesterday, a wild cat walked across the road in front of us, and then it ran into the trees. Dave also loves birds. He has a book about birds, and he has already counted 25 different species. Some of these species only live in the northern states.

On Tuesday, we had our first problem. I got a hole in my back tire. Luckily, Dave knows how to fix a hole, and after 20 minutes we were on the road again.

On Wednesday, we took a boat to Mackinac Island. The boat trip took about 20 minutes. Cars are not allowed on the island, so people get around by bike or by horse. We rode all around the island in 2 hours.

In the evening, we found a small fish restaurant on the corner of Main Street and Lake Street. It is the best restaurant in town. The fish was caught in the lake that morning. Our hotel is on the next corner, so it was a short walk home.

Every night, we secure our bikes with a strong lock outside the hotel. The hotel owner says that the town is very safe, but we want our bikes to be secure.

Tomorrow, we will ride the last part of the route. It might rain. If it rains, we'll stay one more day at the hotel. I'll send you some photos from Dave's camera when we get home.

Love,
Kate

Questions:
Where is Kate writing from?
She is writing from a small hotel in northern Michigan.
Where did Dave mount the camera?
He mounted it on the front of his bike.
How many species of birds has Dave counted?
He has counted 25 different species.
How did they get to Mackinac Island?
They took a boat.
Where is the fish restaurant?
It is on the corner of Main Street and Lake Street.
What will they do if it rains tomorrow?
If it rains, they will stay one more day at the hotel.

lessons.title: My Training Journal
lessons.summary: Nina keeps a journal while she trains for her first 10-mile race.
lessons.text:
March 1
My name is Nina, and today I decided to run the 10-Mile Spring Race in Chicago. The race is on May 20, so I have 11 weeks. My friend Ben has run this race twice, and he told me that I should keep a training journal. So this is my journal.

March 3
Ben said that I should download a running app. This morning, I downloaded one on my mobile phone. The app shows how far I run, how fast I run and my heart rate.

March 10
For my birthday, my parents gave me a smart watch. Now I don't have to carry my mobile phone when I run. The smart watch has a digital map, and it tells me when I am going too fast or too slow.

March 24
It rained for 5 days, and I couldn't run outside. The app said that a week without running is bad for my training. Ben had a good alternative. "Run up and down the steps of your building," he said. It wasn't fun, but it was a good alternative.

April 15
Today I ran 8 miles for the first time! My digital watch said that my heart rate was good.

April 28
I'm sad today. My foot hurts, and the doctor said that I shouldn't run for a week. She told me that rest is critical when your body hurts. I'm sad because I have to stop, but I know she is right. If I rest now, I will still be able to run the race.

May 6
My foot is better. I ran 5 miles today with no pain.

May 19
The race is tomorrow. Ben says that the last day prior to a race is critical. I should eat well, drink a lot of water and go to bed early. Prior to every race, Ben eats a big dinner of fish and potatoes. So tonight, I did the same.

May 20
I did it! I finished the race in 1 hour and 35 minutes. When I crossed the finish line, my smart watch showed 10 miles. I'm going to write about my next race in this journal.

Questions:
Why did Nina start a journal?
Ben told her that she should keep a training journal.
What did Nina download?
She downloaded a running app on her mobile phone.
What did her parents give her for her birthday?
They gave her a smart watch.
What was the alternative when it rained?
She ran up and down the steps of her building.
Why was Nina sad on April 28?
Her foot hurt, and the doctor said that she shouldn't run for a week.
What does Ben eat prior to every race?
He eats a big dinner of fish and potatoes.

lessons.title: The New Coach
lessons.summary: A women's basketball team hires a coach and wins its first game of the new season.
lessons.text:
Megan works in finance at a big bank in Boston. Her job involves a lot of numbers and a lot of meetings, and she sits at her desk for 10 hours a day. Her friend Tina is a lawyer. Being a lawyer is hard too: Tina has to read long documents and go to court.

Every Monday evening, Megan and Tina play basketball in a league for women. Their team is called the Blue Stars. Last season, the Blue Stars suffered 10 losses in 10 games. "We need help," Tina said after the last game.

So the team decided to hire a coach. Megan works in finance, so she was responsible for the team's money. Each player paid $50, and they hired a coach named Linda Park.

Linda has a strong background in basketball. She played for her college team for 4 years, and after that, she coached a high school team for a decade. "With her background, she can really help us," Megan said.

At the first practice, Linda gave each player a responsibility. "Megan, you are fast, so your responsibility is to bring the ball up the court," she said. "Tina, you have a powerful shot, so your responsibility is to take shots from far away." Every player had a clear responsibility.

Linda also explained that winning involves a lot of hard work. A game has 4 quarters of 10 minutes. "Most teams are strong in the first quarter," she said. "But games are won in the fourth quarter." So the team ran a lot at every practice.

In the first game of the new season, the Blue Stars were losing by 2 points after the third quarter. In the fourth quarter, they were stronger than the other team. With 10 seconds left, Tina took a powerful shot from far away, and the ball went in. The Blue Stars won by 1 point.

After the game, the players thanked Linda. "Hiring you was the best idea we ever had," Megan said.

Questions:
What does Megan do?
She works in finance at a big bank in Boston.
What does Tina do?
Tina is a lawyer.
How many losses did the Blue Stars suffer last season?
They suffered 10 losses in 10 games.
Why did Megan think that Linda could help?
She thought so because Linda had a strong background in basketball.
What was Tina's responsibility?
Her responsibility was to take shots from far away, because she had a powerful shot.
What happened in the fourth quarter of the first game?
Tina took a powerful shot, and the Blue Stars won by 1 point.

lessons.title: From Prison to Sports Center
lessons.summary: A small town turns its old prison into a sports center.
lessons.text:
Westfield is a small town in Ohio with about 8,000 residents. In the center of town, there is a large old building made of stone. It was built in 1880, and for more than 100 years, it was a prison. Many criminals were kept there. The walls of the prison were very high, so it was almost impossible to escape.

The prison was closed in 2005. After that, the building was empty for many years. Some residents wanted to destroy it. Other residents wanted to keep it, because it is an important part of the town's history.

Last year, the mayor, Helen Ford, invited the residents to a discussion at the town hall. At the discussion, a representative of a sports company spoke. His name was Mr. Grant. "Our company operates sports centers in 5 states," he said. "We would like to turn the old prison into a sports center, with a pool, a gym and a high wall for climbing."

The first reaction of most residents was very good. Some people had questions. "Who will pay for it?" one woman asked. The representative said that the company would pay for most of the work. One old man said that criminals used to live there, and he didn't want his children to go there. But most residents liked the idea. After a long discussion, they voted, and the plan was accepted.

The work took 2 years. The old prison walls, which were built so that criminals couldn't escape, now have a lot of small colored stones on them for climbing. Kids love them.

The sports center opened last month. The company operates it, and residents of Westfield pay a lower price. At the opening, the mayor spoke to the crowd. "It is an honor to open this center," she said. "This building was a prison for a long time. Now it is a place for health and fun." To honor the history of the building, one room has photos of the old prison.

Questions:
How many residents does Westfield have?
Westfield has about 8,000 residents.
When was the prison built?
It was built in 1880.
Why was it almost impossible to escape from the prison?
It was almost impossible because the walls were very high.
Who spoke at the discussion?
A representative of a sports company spoke.
What was the first reaction of most residents?
The first reaction of most residents was very good.
What did the mayor say at the opening?
She said that it was an honor to open the center.

lessons.title: The Soccer Blog
lessons.summary: Mia writes a blog about her son's soccer team, and a magazine publishes a story about it.
lessons.text:
Mia Lopez has a son named Sam, who is 8 years old. Last fall, Mia became the coach of Sam's soccer team, the Little Tigers. There are 12 children on the team. They practice twice a week in a park near the school, and sometimes in Mia's big back yard.

The Little Tigers were not a strong team. They lost their first 5 games. But Mia had faith in the kids. "We don't have to win," she told them. "We have to try, and we have to have fun."

Mia also started a blog about the team. After every game, she wrote a short post on her blog. In each post, she wrote one sentence about each player. Every sentence was about something good. For example, one sentence was "Ava ran very fast today." Another was "Ben passed the ball well." The parents loved the blog, and the kids loved to read their sentences.

One boy on the team, Leo, has a father who is an actor. Leo's father is not very famous, but a lot of people follow him online. The actor shared the blog with his friends, and soon thousands of people were reading it.

In November, Mia got an email from a magazine for parents. "We love your blog," the email said. "We would like to publish a story about your team in our winter edition." Mia answered the email right away. She said that she was very happy and that she would send some photos.

The winter edition of the magazine came out in December. The story about the Little Tigers was on page 12, with a big photo of the team in Mia's yard. After the publication of the story, Mia got many emails from other parents. They said that the story encouraged them to have faith in their own kids.

The Little Tigers won their last game of the season. That evening, Mia wrote her favorite sentence on the blog: "Everyone on the Little Tigers played well today."

Questions:
Where does the team practice?
They practice in a park near the school, and sometimes in Mia's big back yard.
What did Mia write on her blog after every game?
She wrote one sentence about each player.
Who shared the blog with his friends?
Leo's father, who is an actor, shared it.
What did the email from the magazine say?
It said that the magazine wanted to publish a story about the team in its winter edition.
What happened after the publication of the story?
Mia got many emails from other parents.

lessons.title: The Fitness Test
lessons.summary: Paul has a fitness test at a sports institute, follows the expert's plan and comes back 6 months later.
lessons.text:
Paul is 60 years old, and he has worked as a bus driver for 30 years. Previously, he played soccer every weekend, but now he mostly sits: he sits in his bus all day, and he sits at home in the evening.

His daughter, Emma, works at the Sports Institute at the state university. The institute does research on health and exercise. "Dad, you should come to the institute for a fitness test," Emma said. "It's free for people over 55."

At the institute, an expert named Dr. Lee tested Paul. First, she tested his strength. She tested the strength of his hands, his arms and his back. Then Paul walked on a machine for 10 minutes while the expert watched his heart rate on a computer.

After the test, Dr. Lee explained the results. "Your heart is mostly healthy," she said. "But your strength is low for your age." She said that there is a clear relation between strength and health. "People with more strength stay active for longer. The relation between strength and a long life is very clear."

Then she told Paul about his "body age." "Your actual age is 60," she said. "But your body age is 66. That is the age of your body, not your actual age." Paul was surprised. He asked what he should do. The expert said that he should do strength exercises 3 times a week and walk for 30 minutes every day. She gave him a simple plan.

Paul followed the plan. He mostly did the exercises at home, and he walked to the store instead of driving.

6 months later, Paul came back to the institute. Dr. Lee tested him again to see his progress. His progress was great. His strength was much better, and his body age was now 58, lower than his actual age. "This is real progress," the expert said. Paul laughed. "Previously, my body was older than me," he said. "Now it's younger."

Questions:
What did Paul do on weekends previously?
Previously, he played soccer every weekend.
Where does Emma work?
She works at the Sports Institute at the state university.
What did the expert test first?
She tested his strength.
What did the expert say about strength and health?
She said that there is a clear relation between strength and health.
What was Paul's body age after 6 months?
His body age was 58, lower than his actual age.
Why did Dr. Lee say that it was real progress?
She said so because his strength was much better and his body age was lower.
